subject: Stratos — expedited residency/residency-window request for low-latency onboarding
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@stratos.com>, procurement@stratos.com
Date: 2027-02-21T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Stratos — expedited residency/residency-window request for low-latency onboarding

Team — quick context and an ask from Stratos (enterprise security & ops). They've verbally committed to a 6-month reserved capacity contract if we can guarantee a short-term model residency window and a fallback/residency behavior during onboarding that keeps tail-latency under 200ms for their interactive product.

Key asks from Stratos (attached sheet):
- Short residency window: ability to pin model(s) into their tenant for a prioritized 2-week warm/residency period during go-live.
- Fallback policy: if the tenant hits capacity, auto-fallback to a compatible lower-latency variant (preferably a quantized variant we already have) with transparent routing.
- Auditability: request simple telemetry export (per-route p95/p99) for first 30 days.

Timeline: Stratos wants this capability available in ~2 weeks to hit their onboarding date (they say they'll sign PO if we can commit). Deal is STR-4871; region: US. I've attached the SOW and their latency requirements.

Ask: Can Product + Eng evaluate feasibility and provide an internal prioritization decision (yes/no + high-level implementation approach) by end of day tomorrow? If yes, we will schedule a technical kickoff with Stratos.

Thanks —
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: Stratos_SOW_v2.pdf, latency-requirements.xlsx

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-02-21T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Stratos — expedited residency/residency-window request for low-latency onboarding

Thanks for the context, Marissa. High-level reaction from Eng: doable but there are open questions we need to nail before prioritizing — otherwise risk of rework or SLO misses.

Questions:
- By "pin model(s) into their tenant", do they mean dedicated residency on a subset of GPU capacity (reserved GPUs) or soft residency (routing weight priority + KV cache warm-up)?
- The fallback variant: which model family/version do they consider acceptable? Is quantized LLaMA-2-13B-int8 a candidate, or do they require a trimmed decoder?
- Expected QPS and concurrency during the two-week window? We need concrete token-per-second numbers for capacity planning.
- Security/audit exports: what schema/fields are mandatory for their compliance team? Full logs will require PD review for retention.

If they need dedicated GPUs for a hard pin, lead time is higher (provisioning + infra). Soft residency with routing & prefix caching might be implementable faster but may not hit consistent p99 under heavy burst.

I'll block time with Grace and Ops to sketch a minimal implementation.

— Dev
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
dev_patel@redwood.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@stratos.com>
Date: 2027-02-21T13:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Stratos — expedited residency/residency-window request for low-latency onboarding

Appreciate the fast flag, Marissa. From Product POV: we can present two paths to Stratos — (A) expedited soft-residency + routing + aggressive KV prefill, or (B) committed short-term dedicated residency (higher engineering + infra cost).

Tradeoffs:
- Option A (fast, lower cost): implement routing policy that pins >60% weight to the tenant for 2 weeks, plus a background job to pre-seed KV cache for their top N prefixes. This requires routing policy changes and a cache prefill API; can be done in ~7–10 business days if Eng prioritizes. Does not guarantee dedicated GPU isolation; p99 could still spike under extreme bursts.
- Option B (strong SLA): reserve a small fleet of GPUs and map tenant to that hardware. This delivers the best p99 consistency but requires infra ops & possible billing/commit changes. Provisioning + safety checks ~3 weeks.

For Product to prioritize, we need: committed QPS/concurrency targets (token/sec, % of peak traffic during window), acceptable fallback model(s), and whether short-term dedicated capacity is a hard requirement. Also need the telemetry fields Stratos requires so we can scope the export pipeline.

If Stratos will sign the PO contingent on a 2-week residency capability and can share traffic projections today, I can push this into next sprint planning as a high-priority canary work item.

Grace O'Connor
Principal Product Manager, Platform
grace_oconnor@redwood.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@stratos.com>, procurement@stratos.com
Date: 2027-02-22T08:09:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Stratos — expedited residency/residency-window request for low-latency onboarding

Quick escalation/decision request — leadership note: Stratos is a strategic retail partner (large footprint in US), and they explicitly tied the PO to having the residency/residency-window behavior in place for the go-live. They will commit to a 6-month reserved contract (STR-4871) and provide an initial usage guarantee if we can commit to Option A within 10 business days or Option B within 3 weeks.

I'm asking Product/Eng for a firm internal call: can we accept "Option A" (routing + KV prefill + telemetry export) as a prioritized spike for immediate implementation with an engineering owner? If yes, Marissa will organize a technical kickoff with Stratos today and they'll release the PO within 48 hours. If no, we default to a lower-priority backlog item and risk losing the deal.

Please reply with a concrete "Yes — owner + ETA" or "No — constraints" by EOD today. This is time sensitive; procurement has sign-off ready pending our commitment.

Hannah Schmitt
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

Thanks everyone for the quick responses. Confirming next steps from Sales: Stratos has put the PO on conditional hold pending our ability to commit to Option A within 10 business days. They provided projected steady-state numbers below and uploaded final SOW in DocuSign (link above).

Projected traffic (first 2 weeks):
- Steady QPS: 80 requests/sec (average), spikes to 260 req/sec during peak campaign windows
- Avg tokens per request: 120
- Target p99: <200ms for interactive flows

Customer acceptance criteria:
1) Routing policy in place to prioritize tenant traffic for the 2-week window.
2) KV prefill job completes for top 50 prefixes prior to go-live.
3) Telemetry export (p95/p99 per-route) available within first 7 days.

Marissa will run the kickoff once an owner is identified. Engineering owners: Dev — can you confirm if you can take the spike (Option A) and an ETA (days) for a minimal implementation? Grace — please confirm Product acceptance criteria mapping so we can sign off.

If we lock this today, Stratos will sign PO (STR-4871) and we move to contract.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
